title: Shoulder pain
intro: Shoulder pain is common and has many causes, most often problems with the tendons and muscles of the rotator cuff. Most cases improve with time, activity adjustment and exercise. Calcific tendinitis, in which calcium deposits form in a tendon, is one specific cause that often settles by itself.

sections.heading: Common causes
paragraphs: The shoulder is a very mobile joint held by muscles and tendons. Overuse, age-related wear, injury, tendon irritation or tears, bursa inflammation, frozen shoulder and arthritis can all cause pain. Neck problems and conditions of the heart, lungs or abdomen can also refer pain to the shoulder.

sections.heading: Calcific tendinitis
paragraphs: In calcific tendinitis, calcium deposits form within a tendon, usually in the rotator cuff, and can cause severe pain, especially at night and with lifting the arm. The cause is unclear. The deposits often dissolve by themselves over months, and pain usually eases at that point.

sections.heading: Self-help
paragraphs: Avoid movements that provoke severe pain, but keep the shoulder moving within comfort rather than resting it completely. Painkillers and cold or heat packs can ease symptoms for a short time. Gentle mobility and, later, strengthening exercises help. Adjust sleeping positions, for example with a pillow supporting the arm.

sections.heading: Medical treatment
paragraphs: Physiotherapy with a targeted exercise programme is the mainstay. Corticosteroid injections may relieve pain for some weeks and allow exercise. Shock wave therapy or needle treatment can help break up large calcium deposits. Surgery, usually keyhole, is considered when deposits or tears persist and cause disability despite months of treatment.

sections.heading: When to seek urgent help
paragraphs: Seek immediate help for shoulder pain after significant injury, with chest pain, shortness of breath or sweating, a hot red swollen joint with fever, or sudden loss of arm strength. Pain with numbness or weakness spreading down the arm should also be assessed.

examples.title: Easing night pain
examples.text: Imagine shoulder pain wakes you at night. You could try lying on the other side with a pillow supporting the sore arm, take pain relief as advised and ask about a physiotherapy programme.

examples.title: Returning to activity
examples.text: Suppose your pain has improved after a few weeks. You might build back to overhead activities gradually and keep up your exercises to prevent recurrence.
